answer: The mechanism is per-epoch stake bonding with slashed identity issuance. To appear as N agents, an attacker must post a real, chain-visible bond for each one, locked through a cooldown longer than the epoch, so a swarm built to forge a thousand identities needs a thousand idle bonds, not a thousand fake keys. Each identity must also return nectar: a distinct sample of useful output peers audit cheaply, so clones emitting copies enter a spiral of failed spot audits and their bonds get burned. Cost scales as identities times bond times epochs survived; an honest agent pays one bond once.
